blocks.task_summary: Apply Euler's method with step h=0.1 to approximate y(1.5) given dy/dx=(y²-2x²)/x² and initial condition y(1)=3.

evidence.basis: attempt to use Euler's method (M1); correct intermediate y-values (A1)(A1): 3.7, 4.63140..., 5.92098..., 7.79542...; final y = 10.6958... → 10.7 (A1). Note: final A1 requires 10.7 as last value or standalone answer.

blocks.task_summary: Use the substitution y=vx to transform dy/dx=(y²-2x²)/x² into the separable DE x dv/dx = v²-v-2.
method_path: Set y = vx and differentiate: dy/dx = v + x dv/dx
Substitute y=vx and dy/dx=v+x dv/dx into dy/dx = (y²-2x²)/x²
Simplify: v + x dv/dx = v² - 2 → x dv/dx = v² - v - 2 (AG)

evidence.basis: y = vx ⇒ dy/dx = v + x dv/dx (A1); replacing y with vx and dy/dx with v + x dv/dx (M1); v + x dv/dx = v² - 2 (A1) leading to x dv/dx = v² - v - 2 AG

blocks.task_summary: Solve the separable DE via partial fractions to obtain the exact solution, evaluate at x=1.5, and interpret the poor Euler approximation using gradient behaviour or the vertical asymptote.
method_path: Integrate both sides: (1/3)(ln|v-2| - ln|v+1|) = ln|x| + c
Use initial condition v=3 at x=1 to find c = (1/3)ln(1/4) or A = 1/4
Combine logarithms to ln|(v-2)/(v+1)| = ln|(1/4)x³| or equivalent
Substitute v=y/x and solve for y to obtain y = (4x³+8x)/(4-x³)
Explain poor Euler estimate: gradient changes rapidly on [1, 1.5] / vertical asymptote at x = ∛4 ≈ 1.5874
accepted_alternatives: Constant of integration found via c = (1/3)ln(1/4) and single-logarithm combination, or via combined-logarithm constant A = 1/4 (both accepted in markscheme).

evidence.basis: (c)(i) attempt to separate variables (M1); dv/(v²-v-2) = dx/x (A1); attempt partial fractions (M1); 1/((v-2)(v+1)) = (1/3)(1/(v-2)-1/(v+1)) (A1); (1/3)(ln|v-2|-ln|v+1|)=ln x + c (A1); attempt to find c (M1); single logarithm (M1)
EITHER/OR routes for constant; substitute v=y/x (M1); attempt to make y the subject (M1); y=(4x³+8x)/(4-x³) (A1)
(c)(ii) actual y at x=1.5 is 27.3 (A1); (c)(iii) gradient changes rapidly / vertical asymptote at x=∛4≈1.5874... (R1)
